text:
maya: quick thought  the rule rail is getting bulky when policies have 8+ rules. big cards + scrolling hurts quick scans. what about a compact 'dense' toggle? :thinking:

samir: agreed. biggest issue is chrome (padding + shadow). dense mode could reduce padding, flatten shadows, and hide secondary meta by default. need to keep drag affordances visible though.

olivia: dense toggle makes sense. idea: show an icon row instead of full metadata (region, model, action, rate) and reveal details on hover or focus. keeps info but reduces height.

maya: good call. also keyboard reordering is awkward because the handle is tiny. propose a persistent "Reorder mode" that exposes larger up/down buttons and locks other interactions so accidental drags stop happening.

jess: accessibility nit: when an item is moved via keyboard we must announce with aria-live like "Moved 'Block PII' to position 2". also ensure focus stays on the moved rule. current behavior loses context.

samir: another bug in preview sim: when two rules have identical priority but conflicting actions, the simulator shows both branches but only a toast warns after run. it's easy to miss. we should surface inline validation on the offending rules.

olivia: inline warning pill under the rule title: "priority conflict" with a small tooltip explaining fallback behavior and suggested fixes (e.g., add guard, change priority). keep pill subtle (outline or light bg).

maya: mock addition: tiny heatmap strip in the preview timeline showing rule firing frequency across the sample. hover shows counts; footer contains a tiny legend. low contrast so it doesn't dominate.

jess: heatmap is helpful. design constraints: color contrast >= 3:1 for low-vision; hover counts and ARIA summary for non-visual users so color isn't the only signal. maybe an aria-describedby summarizing top 3 rules by count.

deploy-bot: preview-sim: heatmap strip deployed to staging. run `preview-sim --policy 42 --samples 500` to refresh. logs at /staging/sim/42.

samir: next steps: olivia to iterate mocks (dense toggle + icon row + warning pill), jess to draft aria-live copy and focus rules, maya to write inline warning copy and heatmap tooltip. i'll add an acceptance checklist in the spec. :thumbsup:

olivia: aiming to drop mocks by EOD Friday.

maya: thanks!
